title: GIC and Temasek returns, mandates and NIRC sustainability
asked: MPs asked whether GIC's and Temasek's investment returns are competitive against global benchmarks, whether they have underperformed expectations, how this affects the Net Investment Returns Contribution and CPF/SSGS obligations, and whether their mandates, risk frameworks or public reporting should change.
asked_by: Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Shawn Loh, Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Fadli Fawzi and Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
response: Mr Jeffrey Siow said the Government assesses GIC and Temasek against their own mandates and risk profiles, not other funds. GIC's mandate is to preserve and enhance international purchasing power; it de-risked pre-emptively, which caused some foregone returns, and achieved a 20-year real return of 3.8% per annum. Temasek is an active bottom-up investor without a conventional reference portfolio and reported a 20-year Total Shareholder Return of 8% per annum in US dollar terms. He said NIRC is based on long-term expected returns, not short-term market returns, and the Government can meet CPF/SSGS obligations because of its strong balance sheet.

key_points.point: The Government assesses GIC and Temasek against their own mandates and risk profiles, not other funds.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: The Government assesses GIC and Temasek's performance primarily against their respective mandates and risk profiles, and not with other funds.

key_points.point: GIC's mandate is to preserve and enhance the international purchasing power of assets under its management.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: GIC is the Government's fund manager, and its mandate is to preserve and enhance the international purchasing power of the assets under its management.

key_points.point: GIC's pre-emptive de-risking led to some foregone returns.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: these prudent de-risking measures resulted in some foregone returns.

key_points.point: GIC achieved a 20-year real return of 3.8% per annum.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: GIC has achieved a real return of 3.8% per annum over the past 20 years.

key_points.point: Temasek reported a 20-year Total Shareholder Return of 8% per annum in US dollar terms.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: over the last 20-year period, Temasek has reported a Total Shareholder Return of 8% per annum in US dollar terms.

key_points.point: NIRC is based on the expected long-term real rate of return of the Reserves, not short-term market returns.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: The NIRC is thus derived from the expected long-term real rate of return which the Reserves can sustain, and not short-term market returns.

key_points.point: The Government can meet debt servicing and committed CPF rates through SSGS.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: The Government is able to meet all debt servicing costs and obligations, including the committed CPF rates through the Special Singapore Government Securities (SSGS).

key_points.point: GIC's returns were less volatile and outperformed the reference portfolio on a risk-adjusted basis.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: GIC returns were much less volatile in the same timeframe and in fact, have outperformed the reference portfolio on a risk adjusted basis, given that it has achieved higher returns per unit of volatility.

left_open: Whether GIC's and Temasek's risk-adjusted returns are competitive against appropriate global benchmarks.
How GIC's and Temasek's mandates should evolve to balance capital preservation with higher real returns.
Whether the Government assessed a low-cost passive index-tracking approach and compared it with active management.
Whether MAS's long-term performance and capital allocation framework were reviewed.
Whether the difference between GIC's returns and SSGS interest payments has narrowed, and how the Government would act if GIC's returns consistently underperform SSGS interest rates.
What level of long-term returns would trigger a review of the NIRC framework, and a high-level description of the risk-adjusted metrics GIC uses.
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered NIRC sustainability, CPF/SSGS interest, risk-adjusted returns, public reporting, local infrastructure investment, and Temasek portfolio evaluation.
